content_units: You have   8 weeks  ,   6 hours per week  , and a clear topic list, which is enough for a solid pass with a steady routine. This plan is built for a   first-year business major with low math confidence  , so it emphasizes repetition, worked examples, and short problem sets over heavy theory.
- Priority topics:   journal entries, trial balance, adjusting entries, financial statements, inventory basics
-   2 sessions x 2 hours   for learning + guided examples
-   2 sessions x 1 hour   for practice and recall
- Keep a single   Accounting Error Log  :
- Then solve a similar problem without notes.
- Then explain it aloud in simple words.
Week   Dates   Focus   Key Sessions   Goal/Quiz
1   Sep 25-Oct 1, 2026   Accounting foundations + journal entry basics   Learn account types; debit/credit rules; record 20 basic transactions   Get   75%+   on basic journal-entry drill
2   Oct 2-Oct 8, 2026   Journal entries mastery   Mixed transaction practice; source-doc wording to entries; correct common reversals   Complete 2 timed sets of 15 entries
3   Oct 9-Oct 15, 2026   Posting + trial balance   Post journals to ledger; calculate balances; prepare trial balance; find simple errors   Build 2 full trial balances correctly
4   Oct 16-Oct 22, 2026   Adjusting entries I   Accruals vs deferrals; prepaid expenses; unearned revenue; accrued expenses   Write adjustment type from scenario without prompts
5   Oct 23-Oct 29, 2026   Adjusting entries II + adjusted trial balance   Depreciation basics; accrued revenue; adjusted trial balance flow   Finish one full adjustment set in one sitting
6   Oct 30-Nov 5, 2026   Financial statements   Income statement; statement of owner’s equity/retained earnings; balance sheet; statement order   Prepare statements from adjusted balances
7   Nov 6-Nov 12, 2026   Inventory basics   Perpetual vs periodic overview; COGS basics; ending inventory effects; simple inventory entries   Solve 2 inventory mini-cases correctly
8   Nov 13-Nov 19, 2026   Integration + exam practice   Full-cycle mixed problems; weak-area repair; timed mini-exams   Reach pass mark on 2 mixed mock sets
- Goal: Stop guessing debits and credits.
- Liabilities and equity increase with   credits
- Make a one-page   normal balance sheet
- Say aloud: “What account? Increase or decrease? Which side?”
- Identify accounts and entry direction quickly without panic
- Goal: Turn business events into clean journal entries.
- Use transaction cards such as “paid rent,” “earned cash,” “bought supplies on credit”
- Do   2 untimed sets  , then   2 timed sets
- Rewrite every incorrect entry correctly from memory
- Complete a mixed set with few debit/credit reversals
Week 3: From Journal to Trial Balance
- Goal: Understand the flow, not just isolated entries.
- Post at least   2 full mini-sets   to T-accounts or ledger format
- Check whether total debits = total credits
- Do a short “find the error” exercise
- Circle signs and totals before adding
- Build a clean trial balance from a small set of transactions
- Goal: Understand why end-of-period adjustments are needed.
- what is true at period end?
- If something was used up but not updated, record the expense.
- If something was earned but not recorded, record the revenue.
- Identify adjustment type from wording alone
Week 5: Adjusted Trial Balance + Depreciation Basics
- Goal: Connect adjustments to the final numbers.
- Explain how an adjustment changes accounts and statements
- Goal: Turn adjusted balances into statements.
- Take one adjusted trial balance and prepare all required statements
- putting dividends/drawings on the income statement
- Prepare statements with correct headings and sections
- Goal: Secure easy-to-moderate marks in inventory.
- periodic vs perpetual at a basic level
- Explain inventory flow in plain language
Week 8: Mixed Practice and Exam Readiness
- Do   2 mixed mock sets   under time limits
- Review your Error Log after each set
- Re-do only the questions you missed 24 hours later
- Reach a reliable passing score on mixed practice
Practice Methods That Work Best for Low Math Confidence
Option 1: Worked Example Replay   Copy a solved problem, then cover it and redo it alone   Best for learning process
Option 2: 10-Minute Debit/Credit Drills   Short daily repetition to reduce hesitation   Best for journal entries
Option 3: Error Log Review   Track repeated mistakes and correct patterns weekly   Best for faster improvement
Option 4: Timed Mixed Sets   Simulate exam pressure in small chunks   Best for Weeks 6-8
Use about   1.5-2 hours per day   if possible, with one lighter day before the exam.
- Sort every question by type: prepaid, accrued, unearned, depreciation
- Do 1 mixed mini-case including COGS/inventory effect
- Start with easier journal-entry questions first
- Never leave an adjusting-entry question blank if you can identify the accounts involved
